Find files in a project that look like SRTR data

Source: R/check_repo_for_srtr_data.R
check_repo_for_srtr_data.Rd

Scans a project folder for files that look like SRTR standard analysis file (SAF) data and that could be committed to git. It applies the same three rules as the check that runs on sRtr's own repository on GitHub:

  • Data formats: files in the formats SAFs come in or are converted to (.sas7bdat, .sas7bcat, .xpt, .parquet, .feather, .arrow, .dta, .sav), in any letter case.

  • Identifier columns: .csv, .tsv and .txt files whose first line names an SRTR identifier column (TRR_ID, TRR_FOL_ID, PX_ID, PERS_ID, DONOR_ID, CAN_ID, TX_ID or REC_ID). Files under tests/testthat/fixtures/ whose names start with synthetic- are skipped, as in sRtr's own repository.

  • Large files: any file over 5 MB, which may hold data in another format.

The scan only reads: it lists files and reads the first line of text files. It changes nothing.

Usage

check_repo_for_srtr_data(path = ".", files = NULL, staged = FALSE)

Arguments

path

The project folder to scan. Defaults to the working directory.

files

Optional. Paths of files to check, relative to path, instead of the file list described under "Which files are scanned". Files that do not exist are skipped.

staged

If TRUE, check the files staged for the next commit in the git repository that holds path, as they are staged rather than as they are in the folder. Paths in the result are then relative to the top of the repository. This is what use_srtr_commit_check()'s hook runs. Cannot be used with files.

Value

A tibble with one row per finding, returned invisibly: path (relative to the folder scanned), problem ("data format", "identifier column", "unreadable file" or "large file") and detail. A text file whose first line cannot be read is reported as unreadable rather than passed as clean. A file can appear more than once. The scan warns, naming the paths only, when it finds anything, and gives a message when it finds nothing.

Which files are scanned

In a git repository, the scan covers the files git would commit: tracked files and untracked files that .gitignore does not exclude. A SAF that is ignored is not reported. When path is not in a git repository, or git is not installed, every file under path is scanned, except those in hidden folders such as .git.

The scan finds the usual formats and headers only. It does not find SRTR data saved as .rds or .RData files, or text files without an identifier column, so an empty result is not proof that a project holds no SRTR data. See the data protection guide.

Check when sRtr is attached

When you call library(sRtr) from inside a git repository, sRtr runs the same scan on that repository and shows a short message, naming paths only, if it finds files git would commit that look like SRTR data. The message also says when the repository's ignore rules do not cover every SAF format (use_srtr_gitignore() adds them) and when no commit check is installed (use_srtr_commit_check()). Nothing is shown when there is nothing to report. set_srtr_wd() warns when the SAF folder itself is inside a git repository and not ignored.

Turn both checks off with options(sRtr.safety_check = FALSE), for example in your .Rprofile. The attach message is a package startup message, so suppressPackageStartupMessages() hides it too. Both are skipped during R CMD check, and the attach check is skipped while a document is being knitted, so its message never appears in a report.

See also

Other data protection: use_srtr_gitignore()

Examples

# A made-up project with one file that looks like data
project <- file.path(tempdir(), "made-up-project")
dir.create(project, showWarnings = FALSE)
writeLines("TRR_ID,AGE", file.path(project, "cohort.csv"))
writeLines("x <- 1", file.path(project, "analysis.R"))

findings <- check_repo_for_srtr_data(project)
#> Warning: 1 file looks like SRTR data and could be committed from
#> /tmp/RtmprydEfS/made-up-project (folder scan; not a git repository):
#> • cohort.csv (identifier column)
#> ℹ Move SAFs and files made from them out of the project, or add them to
#>   .gitignore.
findings
#> # A tibble: 1 × 3
#>   path       problem           detail
#>   <chr>      <chr>             <chr> 
#> 1 cohort.csv identifier column TRR_ID

unlink(project, recursive = TRUE)
